workflows.name: Verify ID uploads against form data with PDF Vector, Airtable and Slack

user.name: PDF Vector
user.bio: A fully featured PDF APIs for developers - Parse any PDF or Word document, extract structured data, and access millions of academic papers - all through simple APIs.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Applicants upload a passport, driver license or ID card through an n8n form. PDF Vector reads it, the workflow checks name, date of birth and expiry against the form, logs the result in Airtable and asks a reviewer in Slack when something is off.

How it works
An n8n Form Trigger asks for full name, date of birth, email and one ID file (PDF, JPG or PNG).
The PDF Vector node runs the identity extractor on the file and returns document type, full name, date of birth, document number, issuing country and expiry date as JSON.
A Code node compares the document with the form. Every word of the typed name must appear in the name on the document (accents and case are ignored), the birth dates must be equal, and the expiry date must be at least minDaysBeforeExpiry days away.
One Airtable row is created per upload with the extracted values, only the last four characters of the document number, a status of Passed checks or Needs review, and the reasons. Each submission adds a new row, so an applicant who uploads again after a failed read or a review gets a second row with the same email.
Uploads that need review are posted to Slack with a link to the Airtable row, where the reviewer sets the status. If PDF Vector cannot read the file or Airtable rejects the row, Slack gets a message with the applicant's email and the error.

Setup
Install the verified community node n8n-nodes-pdfvector (tested with version 2.1.15 on n8n 2.46) and add a PDF Vector credential with an API key from app.pdfvector.com.
Create an Airtable table with these columns: Applicant (text), Email (email), Document type (text), Name on document (text), Date of birth (date), Document number (last 4) (text), Issuing country (text), Expiry date (date), Status (single select with Passed checks, Needs review, Approved and Rejected), Problems (long text), Submitted at (date and time).
Add Airtable and Slack credentials and invite the Slack app to the review channel.
Open Set your configuration and paste the base ID (starts with app) and table ID (starts with tbl) from the table URL, and the Slack channel ID. Activate the workflow and send applicants the production form URL.

Requirements
PDF Vector account and API key (each document uses credits)
Airtable base for the check log
Slack workspace for review requests and failure alerts
n8n with the n8n-nodes-pdfvector community node

Customization
Change minDaysBeforeExpiry to require a longer validity, for example 180 days for travel or rental checks
Add a Gmail or Outlook node on the review branch to ask the applicant for a new upload
Add fields to the JSON schema in the PDF Vector node, such as address or nationality, and map them to new Airtable columns

Additional info
This is a first-pass consistency check, not identity verification: it does not detect forged documents or confirm that the person uploading is the holder. Strict name matching sends nicknames, transliterated names and missing middle names to review. n8n stores uploaded files in execution data, so turn off saving successful executions if you must not keep ID copies.

workflows.name: Verify phone numbers and save leads with iBlueText and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow collects a lead’s name, phone number, and optional email via an n8n form, verifies the phone using iBlueText (iMessage or SMS), then appends or updates the verified lead in Google Sheets and sends a welcome text via iBlueText.

How it works
Starts when a user submits the first n8n Form with their name, mobile number, and optional email.
Normalizes the submitted phone number into international format and prepares a configurable welcome message.
Calls the iBlueText Verify API to send a 6-digit verification code and, if sending fails, shows an error completion page.
Prompts the user for the code in a second form and checks it against iBlueText.
If the code is wrong, prompts once more and re-checks the code, then ends with a “wrong/expired code” completion page if verification still fails.
When verification succeeds, formats a verified lead payload, appends or updates the record in Google Sheets matching on phone number, and sends a personalized welcome SMS/iMessage via iBlueText.
Shows a final “verified” completion page to the user.

Setup
Create an iBlueText account, generate an API key, and add an n8n HTTP Header Auth credential using Authorization: Bearer  for the iBlueText requests.
Create a Google Sheets OAuth credential in n8n and select the target spreadsheet and sheet in the Google Sheets append/update step.
Ensure your Google Sheet has columns for name, phone, email, channel, and verified_at, and keep phone as the matching key to prevent duplicates.
Update the default country code logic (if needed) in the phone-normalization step and edit the welcome message text to match your brand.
Activate the workflow and share the n8n form URL for the initial phone number collection form.

Requirements
An iBlueText account (free to start, first 10 verifications free) and an API key. A Sandbox test key (sk-ibt-test-) lets you test without texting anyone; the code is always 000000.
A Google Sheets account and a sheet with the headers name, phone, email, channel, verified_at.
For the welcome text: a sending line on your iBlueText account (a free trial line works). Codes themselves go out from iBlueText's own numbers.

Customization
Change the welcome text in Your settings; {first_name} becomes the lead's first name. Keep it a question with no link for the best reply rate.
Set your default country code (DEFAULT_CC) in Clean phone number, e.g. '+44' or '+61'.
Swap Save lead to Google Sheets for your CRM (HubSpot, Airtable, Notion...) or add more fields to the first form page.
Edit the form titles and the verified, wrong-code and couldn't-send pages to match your brand.

workflows.name: Verify scraped lead emails with Apify and Google Sheets

user.name: Edge
user.bio: I build n8n workflows that find and qualify local-business leads with official APIs. Free templates here; the full Lead List Builder is on my Gumroad.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs manually or on a weekly schedule to verify scraped lead emails using Apify’s Bulk Email Verifier, sourcing leads from either a Google Sheet or an Apify dataset, and then writes verification results back to Google Sheets or splits them into new Apify datasets by verdict.

How it works
Runs manually or every Monday at 08:00.
Checks the Settings to decide whether to process an Apify dataset ID or read leads from a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
When using Google Sheets, reads rows where the email status is empty or set to “unknown”, extracts email addresses from the email column, and batches them up to the configured limits.
Runs the Apify “Bulk Email Verifier: syntax, MX, disposable, role and typo” Actor to verify the emails and retrieve the results dataset.
If the input came from Google Sheets, matches verification results back to each sheet row and updates the sheet with “Email status”, “Best email”, and “Email notes”.
If the input came from an Apify dataset, groups results by verdict (valid/risky/invalid/unknown), creates a new Apify dataset per verdict, and uploads the corresponding rows.

Setup
Install the community node package @apify/n8n-nodes-apify in your n8n instance.
Create an Apify API credential in n8n and select it for the Apify Actor node and the Apify HTTP Request nodes.
If using Google Sheets as the source, add a Google Sheets OAuth credential, set the document ID and sheet name in both Google Sheets nodes, and ensure your sheet has columns matching the configured email and status headers (for example “Email” and “Email status”).
If using an Apify dataset as the source, paste the dataset ID (or dataset URL) into apifyDatasetId in Settings and confirm the correct emailField name for items in that dataset.
Review the Settings values (for example maxEmails, batchSize, timeoutSeconds, and optional checkSmtp) to fit your volume and verification strictness before activating the schedule.

Requirements
n8n with the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify (tested with version 0.9.0 on n8n 2.45.5). Install guide: https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/
An Apify account and its API token (Apify Console, Settings, Integrations)
Google Sheets access, only for the sheet route

Customization
Raise maxEmails or batchSize in Settings to check more addresses per execution
Turn on checkSmtp to also probe the mailbox (slower, and many mail servers block the probe)
Change resultDatasetPrefix to name the new result datasets your way

Additional info
Cost: the Bulk Email Verifier Actor is pay per event on Apify: $0.0006 per address with a verdict (valid, risky or invalid), free for status unknown, plus $0.00005 per run start (prices read 6 Nov 2026). Valid means the domain accepts mail; the mailbox itself is probed only with checkSmtp on. Actor page: https://apify.com/edgef-4/bulk-email-verifier

workflows.name: Verify email contacts in Google Sheets with EmailAwesome
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This manual workflow verifies a single email address stored in Google Sheets using EmailAwesome, saving a provider validation ID and later retrieving the verification status back into the same row with state, result, timestamp, and notes.

How it works
Starts manually and reads the target spreadsheet ID, tab name, row ID, and run mode (preview or live).
Looks up the selected contact row in Google Sheets by its row_id and validates that required columns and a plausible email address are present.
If running in preview mode or the row is not in an actionable state, stops and returns a message without calling EmailAwesome or writing to Google Sheets.
When the row is READY, reserves the row in Google Sheets to prevent accidental retries, then submits the email address to EmailAwesome to start a validation.
Confirms the EmailAwesome response matches the selected email, then writes the returned validation_id to Google Sheets and sets the row state to PENDING.
When the row is PENDING with an existing validation_id, fetches the validation from EmailAwesome, maps the provider status to DONE, PENDING, or REVIEW, and writes the result, checked timestamp, and note back to Google Sheets.

Setup
Create a Google Sheets spreadsheet with a Contacts tab (or update the tab name) that includes the columns row_id, email, state, validation_id, result, checked_at, and note.
Add a Google Sheets credential in n8n and attach it to all Google Sheets steps, then paste your spreadsheet ID and choose a row_id in the Setup step.
Add your EmailAwesome API key as Header Auth for both EmailAwesome MCP steps using header name x-api-key.
Start with mode set to preview to validate the row selection, then switch to live only when you are ready to submit an authorized email for verification.

Additional info
EmailAwesome API setup and documentation

workflows.name: Verify lead emails from websites with Apify and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow reads lead website URLs from Google Sheets or accepts a URL list from another workflow, extracts emails with Apify Contact Details Extractor, verifies them with Apify Email Verifier, and then either appends the results to Google Sheets or returns the verified rows to the caller.

How it works
Starts either manually (to process a Google Sheets list) or when invoked by another workflow/agent with a pageUrls input array.
Collects and de-duplicates valid http(s) page URLs from the Google Sheets “Leads” tab (column website/url) or from the inbound pageUrls input.
Sends the page URLs to Apify (skilled_glee/contact-details-extractor) to extract contact information, including any emails found on each page.
De-duplicates extracted emails and keeps the first source page URL where each email was found.
Sends the unique email list to Apify (skilled_glee/email-verifier) to check syntax, DNS/MX, disposable/role/free-provider flags, and typo suggestions (no SMTP mailbox check).
Formats one output row per email with the verdict, reasons, and metadata, and either appends the rows to the Google Sheets “Verified” tab or returns them to the calling workflow.

Setup
Add an Apify API token as HTTP Header Auth using Authorization: Bearer  for both Apify HTTP requests.
Add a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential and select the target spreadsheet in both Google Sheets nodes.
Create a “Leads” sheet tab with a website (or url) column containing one http(s) page URL per row, ideally a contact page.
Create a “Verified” sheet tab with header columns: website, email, verdict, reasons, dnsStatus, mxProvider, disposable, role, freeProvider, didYouMean, mailboxVerified, checkedBy, checkedAt.
If calling this workflow from another workflow/agent, pass pageUrls as an array of http(s) URLs and note that results are returned to the caller and not written to Google Sheets.

Additional info
What it checks: syntax, domain MX / null MX / NXDOMAIN, disposable domain, role account, free provider, typo hint → pass / risky / fail. It does NOT connect to mail servers and does NOT confirm a mailbox exists (mailboxVerified is always false). Contact extraction is one page per URL over plain HTTP with pattern matching — review results. Cost (Apify pay-per-event, billed to your Apify token): $0.0015 per page processed + $0.001 per unique email checked. Each Actor call capped at $0.25 via maxTotalChargeUsd. Store: https://apify.com/skilled_glee/email-verifier · https://apify.com/skilled_glee/contact-details-extractor

workflows.name: Verify Polish VAT White List supplier accounts with forms and Data Tables
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow provides an n8n form to validate a supplier’s NIP and bank account, checks them against Poland’s Ministry of Finance VAT White List API, and logs each verification (including requestId) to an n8n Data Table before showing a pay/no-pay verdict to the user.

How it works
Receives a submission from an n8n Form with the supplier NIP, bank account number, invoice number, and gross amount in PLN.
Normalizes the inputs and validates the NIP checksum and the Polish bank account number checksum (NRB/PL IBAN).
If the input is invalid, displays a form completion message listing the validation errors.
If the input is valid, calls the Poland VAT White List (wykazpodatnikowvat.mf.gov.pl) API to retrieve the supplier’s VAT status and check whether the bank account is assigned to the NIP for today’s date.
Combines the API responses into a verdict (OK/NOT_ON_LIST/NOT_FOUND/CHECK/ERROR) and builds a user-facing explanation including the official requestId when available.
Writes an audit record of the check to an n8n Data Table and then displays the verdict and details back to the form submitter.

Setup
Run the manual “create the checks table” trigger once to create the vat_whitelist_checks n8n Data Table.
Activate the workflow and share the production URL of the n8n Form used for payment checks.
Optionally adjust the API base URL, timezone, and the large-payment threshold (default 15,000 PLN) in the workflow settings values.

Requirements
An n8n instance with Data Tables and multi-page Forms (recent n8n version, cloud or self-hosted)
Internet access to the public VAT White List API of the Polish Ministry of Finance (no API key or account needed)

Customization
Send NOT_ON_LIST and CHECK results to Slack, email or Telegram so the person approving payments is alerted.
Replace the form with a Google Sheets or accounting-system trigger to check a whole list of pending payments.
Add the requestId to your bank transfer export or payment description to keep the proof of the check next to the payment.
Change the large-payment threshold and timezone in the Settings node.

Additional info
The White List API is free but has daily query limits per IP address; check the current limits on the Ministry of Finance website before using it at scale.
The API moved to https://wykazpodatnikowvat.mf.gov.pl/api on 15 October 2026. The base URL is a single value in the Settings node, so it is easy to update.
Only accounts of active VAT payers are listed. This workflow is a due-diligence helper, not tax or legal advice.

workflows.name: Verify Google Sheets lead emails with Apify Email Verifier
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Automatically verify email addresses in your Google Sheets lead list before launching campaigns. This workflow identifies unverified contacts, validates them in batches via SMTP handshake, catch-all and disposable checks, and writes detailed verdicts back to your spreadsheet. 

How it works
Reads unverified rows: Fetches leads from Google Sheets where the status column is empty, ensuring scheduled runs only process new contacts.
Deduplicates and batches: Cleans whitespace, drops duplicate addresses to avoid duplicate charges, and groups emails into batches of 100.
Live verification: Sends batches to the Apify Email Verifier API to perform syntax, MX, disposable, and SMTP catch-all checks without sending any emails.
Maps verdicts back: Matches verification responses by email address (handling case-insensitivity and email tags) to maintain sheet integrity even when results return reordered.
Updates sheet: Writes the final status, sub-status, quality score, catch-all flag, and disposable flag back to the matching row.

Setup
Google Sheet preparation: Add the following column headers to your sheet: email, status, sub_status, score, catch_all, disposable, verified_at. Only the email column needs lead data.
Apify credential: In n8n, navigate to Credentials > New > Header Auth. Name it Apify API, set Header Name to Authorization, and set Header Value to Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN (obtain from console.apify.com).
Connect Google Sheets: Open both Google Sheets nodes ("Read Unverified Rows in Sheets" and "Update Sheets with Verdicts"), authenticate your Google account, and select your target document and sheet.
Execute: Click "Test workflow" to verify your unverified leads and view live results populated in your spreadsheet.

Requirements
Google Sheets account and credentials connected in n8n.
Apify account with an API token (free tier available with monthly credits).
An n8n Header Auth credential named "Apify API".

Customization
Change batch size: In the "Filter and Batch Rows" node, adjust BATCH_SIZE (default: 100) based on your list size and Apify plan.
Custom column names: If your spreadsheet uses different header names, update EMAIL_COLUMN and STATUS_COLUMN constants in the Code nodes.
Schedule trigger: Replace the "Manual Execution Trigger" node with a Schedule Trigger to run automated lead list cleaning on a recurring basis.

Additional info
• Cost: Uses the pay-per-event Apify Actor (sumitr_mardy/email-verifier). Free tier available.
• Open-source repository, documentation, and additional templates (CSV cleaner, Signup webhook, AI agent tool): https://github.com/sumitrmardy/email-verifier-api

workflows.name: Log and verify Qersh wallet transfers via webhooks to Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives signed Qersh wallet-transfer webhooks, verifies the request signature, and logs new incoming transfers to Google Sheets while avoiding duplicates by delivery ID and updating existing rows when a suspected forgery verdict arrives.

How it works
Receives a POST webhook from Qersh containing a raw JSON delivery and signature headers.
Verifies the X-Qersh-Signature HMAC against the raw body using your connection key and rejects invalid requests with a 401 response.
Immediately returns a 200 OK response for valid deliveries, then stops processing if the event is a connection test.
Checks whether the event is a new incoming transfer (transfer.received) or an update event.
For transfer.received events, looks up the delivery_id in Google Sheets and appends a new row only if it is not already logged.
For update events flagged as suspected forgery, updates the matching Google Sheets row (by transfer_id) to set the status to “SUSPECTED FORGERY”.

Setup
Replace the placeholder connection_key value in the Settings step with the Qersh connection key shown on the phone.
Create or choose a Google Sheet with columns for received_at, amount, currency, payer_number, payer_name, provider_txn_id, wallet, risk, auto_confirm_ok, transfer_id, delivery_id, and status.
Add a Google Sheets credential in n8n and select the target document and sheet in the Google Sheets read/append/update steps.
Activate the workflow and paste the Webhook Production URL into the Qersh app as your store URL.
If self-hosting n8n, set NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN=crypto so the signature verification code can use the crypto module.

Requirements
The Qersh app on the merchant's Android phone (it sends the signed webhook); a Google account with a sheet; self-hosted n8n with NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN=crypto, or n8n Cloud.

Customization
Add columns to the append step (for example balance_after or the payer handle). Keep 'Send sender details' on 'full name and number' in the wallet, or the payer number arrives masked.

Additional info
Qersh (Qersh Pay) is a wallet notification relay, not a payment service provider: no money passes through Qersh or through n8n; the phone only tells your workflow that a transfer arrived. The phone retries a failed delivery for days, so a Sheets outage loses nothing. Docs: https://qersh.cfd/en/integrations/n8n . The Qersh community node (@qersh-pay/n8n-nodes-qersh) does the same with an encrypted credential.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Monitor a signed crypto price from the Pulse Verity Index on a schedule. Verify record integrity, apply your own freshness and quality requirements, record decisions in n8n Data Tables, and receive Slack alerts when a failure changes or service recovers.

How it works
Run manually for setup or every ten minutes for one configured crypto symbol.
Validate the symbol and example consumer policy, then call get_index_price through the hosted MCP endpoint using your Bearer Auth credential.
Preserve the complete signed record and call verify_print. Require verification of the exact full record before evaluating its quality.
Evaluate observation age, future timestamps, grade, confidence, dispersion and source count against your configured consumer policy. Unavailable responses, timeouts and invalid verification produce an UNAVAILABLE outcome.
Write a compact decision audit to n8n Data Tables and compare it with the persistent prior state. Repeated unchanged notifications are suppressed; an initial healthy check establishes a quiet baseline.
Send Slack alerts for initial failures, changed failure reasons or policies, and recovery. Persist notification state after Slack succeeds. An interrupted delivery can still duplicate a later alert.

Setup
Import while inactive. Create a developer key at https://thepulse.markets/developers and select an n8n Bearer Auth credential in both MCP nodes. Never paste credentials into the workflow JSON.
Create the two n8n Data Tables using the exact schemas in the workflow canvas notes, and select them in the corresponding nodes. Select your Slack OAuth credential and destination channel.
Review the symbol and illustrative consumer thresholds, test manually, then activate a cadence that fits your account limits. Run one execution at a time and configure audit retention and project access.

Requirements
n8n with MCP Client, Code, Schedule Trigger, Data Tables and Slack nodes; a Pulse Verity developer key and Slack credentials. Import/export compatibility was checked with n8n 2.42.6. No AI model or community node is required.

Customization
Configure the symbol, consumer freshness and quality policy, table selections and Slack channel. The example thresholds are consumer preferences, not disclosures of the proprietary Verity engine.

Additional info
Signatures establish record integrity, not price correctness. The hosted verifier is trusted over HTTPS. This operations monitor does not trade or authorize settlement. Slack delivery and state persistence are not atomic; an interrupted delivery can duplicate a later notification. Workflow retries and saved execution payloads are disabled. Instance logs follow hosting policy. Audit rows require retention management. Verity account limits and n8n hosting costs apply.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Verify a phone number or email lead before updating your CRM. This Zelnum realtime workflow checks current products, previews pricing without a charge, and requires explicit billing approval before returning per-product verdicts and spending details.

How it works
Runs manually to start a verification request for one phone number or email address.
Fetches Zelnum’s current realtime product catalog to ensure the selected product IDs exist and match the chosen series (phone or email).
Validates the input identifier, country (for phone), product selection, and billing controls, then requests a non-billable quote from the Zelnum realtime quote endpoint.
Checks the quote total and expiry and branches based on whether billing is explicitly enabled.
If billing is not enabled, returns a quote-only preview (no charge) so you can review pricing.
If billing is enabled and within the max USDT limit, submits the billable realtime check to Zelnum using an idempotency key and the quote token.
Parses the Zelnum response into CRM-friendly output including overall verification_state and per-product results with valid/invalid/unknown verdicts and billing status.

Setup
Register with Zelnum, open API Center, and create an API key. Add an n8n HTTP Header Auth credential with header name X-API-Key and your private key, then select it on the quote and billable check HTTP Request nodes. Never publish the key or real contact data.
In the configuration step, set series (phone or email), the identifier, and (for phone) a two-letter country code when using a national number.
Run once to inspect the product catalog output, then set 1–10 matching Zelnum realtime product_ids for the chosen series.
To run paid checks, set a stable idempotency_key, set max_total_usdt, and change execute_billable to true after reviewing the quote preview.
Add your downstream CRM/database nodes after the final output to store or route the verdicts (for example, flag manual_review items for follow-up).

Requirements
A Zelnum account with API access, sufficient balance for paid checks, and compatible built-in n8n nodes. Run quote previews first; keep execute_billable=false until you approve the price.

Customization
After private testing, connect your CRM or an authenticated form trigger. Route inconclusive results to manual review rather than treating them as invalid.

Additional info
Read the Zelnum API documentation for product coverage, billing, and error codes. Visit Zelnum for the platform overview. Product verdicts do not establish contact consent or guarantee email deliverability.

workflows.description:
Proof of delivery that checks itself. This workflow collects driver submissions from an n8n Form, matches each waybill against your Google Sheets deliveries register, verifies the uploaded photo with OpenAI vision (gpt-5.6-terra), and confirms the delivery or raises an exception through Gmail and Telegram.

Last updated: September 2026.

Quick Overview
This workflow captures proof-of-delivery submissions via an n8n Form, matches them against a Google Sheets deliveries register, verifies uploaded photos with OpenAI vision, logs outcomes to Google Sheets, and sends confirmations or exception alerts through Gmail and Telegram.

How it works
Receives a driver submission from an n8n Form with waybill/order number, recipient name, optional notes, and an optional delivery photo.
Normalizes the submission, generates a POD ID, and flags whether a usable photo file is attached.
If the waybill is missing, it emails the ops inbox via Gmail and posts an alert to Telegram, then stops processing.
Looks up the submitted waybill in a Google Sheets “Deliveries” register and, if not found, appends an “Unrecognized waybill” entry to a Google Sheets “PodLog” sheet and alerts ops via Gmail and Telegram.
If the waybill exists but no photo is provided, it logs a “no photo” exception to Google Sheets and notifies ops via Gmail and Telegram.
If a photo is provided, it sends the image and context to OpenAI (gpt-5.6-terra) to classify the proof as “ok” or “mismatch” and return a short summary.
When the photo is verified as ok, it updates the matching delivery row in Google Sheets to “Delivered,” logs the verified result to “PodLog,” emails the customer via Gmail, and posts a confirmation to Telegram.
When the photo is flagged as mismatch, it logs an exception to “PodLog” and alerts ops via Gmail and Telegram for manual review.

Setup
Add credentials for Google Sheets OAuth2, Gmail OAuth2, Telegram Bot API, and OpenAI API.
Create (or update) a Google Sheets document with two tabs named “Deliveries” (including a waybill column and customer_name/customer_email/status/assigned_date fields) and “PodLog” (to store log_id, waybill, status, signal, recipient, notes, and timestamps).
Update the Google Sheets document ID (and sheet names if different) in all Google Sheets steps that read “Deliveries” and append to “PodLog.”
Set the ops notification targets by updating the Gmail recipient address(es) and the Telegram chat ID used for alerts.
For the form intake, publish the n8n Form and share it with drivers (and ensure file uploads are enabled for images).

Quick Answers
What counts as valid proof of delivery?
A photo that plausibly shows a delivery scene, such as a parcel, box, package, entrance, doorstep, or a person receiving goods. Blurry, black, or unrelated images like selfies, receipts, and screenshots get flagged for manual review.

What happens when the waybill is unknown?
An “Unrecognized waybill” row is appended to the PodLog sheet and ops is alerted via Gmail and Telegram.

What if the driver forgets the photo?
A “no photo” exception is logged to Google Sheets and ops is notified via Gmail and Telegram, so the delivery is not marked as done.

When does the delivery row change?
Only after the photo is verified as ok does the matching row in the Deliveries sheet get updated to “Delivered,” followed by a customer confirmation email and a Telegram post.

user.name: Searchbug
user.bio: Automation builder focues on data enrichment, verification, and compliance. My templates connect Searchbug's people-search, contact, and validation APIs to n8n forms, Google Sheet, and Slack. Helping teams verify leads, clean CRM data, and stay TCPA/FCRA-aware without writing code.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow collects a single email or a CSV upload via an n8n form, verifies each address with the Searchbug Email Verification API, appends the results to Google Sheets, and posts a valid/invalid count summary to a Slack channel.

How it works
Receives a submission from an n8n form that includes either a single email address or an uploaded CSV file.
Routes the run to single-email processing or parses the uploaded CSV into one item per row.
Normalizes each record to a consistent email field regardless of CSV header capitalization.
Verifies each email by calling the Searchbug Email Verification API and continues even if some requests error.
Extracts key fields (status, domain, MX, SMTP provider, and related flags) into a clean result object.
Appends each verification result as a new row in a Google Sheets tab.
Aggregates totals (valid/invalid/total) and posts a summary message to Slack.

Setup
Add your Searchbug credentials by filling in the CO_CODE and PASS query parameters in the HTTP request to Searchbug.
Connect your Google Sheets account, set your target spreadsheet and the “Email Verification” sheet (or update the document and sheet names), and ensure the header columns match the fields being appended.
Connect your Slack account and select the channel where the workflow posts the verification summary.
If you submit CSV files, ensure the uploaded file is a .csv and includes an email column (any of email, Email, or EMAIL works).

workflows.name: Verify AppsMax lead webhooks and forward new leads to an external HTTPS API
workflows.description:
Quick overview

This workflow verifies AppsMax application webhooks with HMAC-SHA256 and forwards only new application.created leads to an external HTTPS API. AppsMax receives success only after the destination returns 2xx.

How it works

The Webhook node receives a POST request from AppsMax and preserves the raw request body.
Crypto calculates HMAC-SHA256 for the raw payload. Code compares it with the lowercase-hex X-Appsmax-Signature header.
An invalid signature returns 401 without processing the payload.
The event filter accepts only application.created. Other valid events, including application.test, return 204 without calling the destination.
Edit Fields selects the minimum lead data and creates a stable idempotency key from the event and application state.
HTTP Request posts the JSON payload with Idempotency-Key and X-Appsmax-Event headers.
A downstream 2xx returns 200 to AppsMax. A 4xx, 5xx, timeout, or network failure returns 502, allowing the AppsMax delivery policy to retry.

Setup

In AppsMax, enable an outgoing application webhook and copy the n8n production webhook URL into its endpoint setting.
Replace the placeholder webhook path with a long random value, then update the URL in AppsMax.
Create an n8n Crypto credential, put the AppsMax webhook secret only in its HMAC Secret field, and attach it to the HMAC node.
Replace example.invalid with an HTTPS endpoint you control. Configure destination authentication through an n8n credential, not in the URL or workflow JSON.
Make the destination handle Idempotency-Key atomically and return 2xx for both a newly accepted event and an already accepted replay.
Before activation, test a valid event, an invalid signature, application.test, a downstream failure, and a replay with synthetic data.

Requirements

An AppsMax project with an outgoing application webhook enabled
n8n with the standard Webhook, Crypto, Code, If, Edit Fields, HTTP Request, and Respond to Webhook nodes
A controlled HTTPS endpoint that accepts JSON and deduplicates repeated requests

Customization

Extend Edit Fields when the destination needs more application attributes.
Add routing by lead source or status after the signature and event checks.
Replace the generic HTTP destination with a CRM, ERP, help desk, or internal API while preserving the idempotency and response gates.

Additional info

This free template uses only standard n8n nodes; it is not a native AppsMax node. It contains no credential IDs, tokens, webhook secrets, or client data. Keep the workflow inactive until the test matrix passes. The AppsMax-side steps are documented in the AppsMax n8n guide.

workflows.name: Verify tax IDs in PDF uploads with Groq, Google Sheets, Lovable, and Gmail

user.name: Chijioke Ogbonna
user.bio:
Chijioke is an AI Automation Engineer with 2+ years of experience designing end-to-end workflows, API integrations, and intelligent automation solutions with n8n. I specialize in building scalable pipelines that save costs, reduce manual effort, and deliver measurable business outcomes. 

My portfolio includes fraud detection systems, compliance automation, and communication workflows across SaaS, fintech, and enterprise operations.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives tax document PDFs from a Lovable form webhook, extracts and parses the Tax ID with Groq, validates and matches it against a Google Sheets “TaxID_Database,” logs results to Google Sheets, emails the submitter via Gmail, and returns a JSON verdict back to Lovable.

How it works
Receives a POST webhook from Lovable containing a base64-encoded PDF and submitter metadata.
Generates a request ID, normalizes the incoming fields, and checks Google Sheets “Verification_Log” for a recent run with the same filename to return a cached duplicate result.
If not a duplicate, extracts readable text from the PDF payload and sends it to Groq (OpenAI-compatible chat completions) to parse the tax ID and document details as JSON.
If no tax ID is extracted, immediately returns a JSON error response to Lovable indicating that no tax ID was found.
Validates and normalizes the extracted tax ID format, then looks it up in the Google Sheets “TaxID_Database” to determine match score, entity mismatch, and a preliminary verification status.
Sends the combined verification facts to Groq to produce a final compliance verdict with risk level, score, flags, summary, and recommended action.
Appends the full verification audit record to Google Sheets, updates the matched database row or logs unknown tax IDs, emails the submitter the outcome via Gmail, and responds to Lovable with the final JSON result.

Setup
Configure the Lovable form (or other source) to POST to this workflow’s webhook URL and include at least pdf_base64, file_name, submitted_by, email, and organization fields.
Add Groq authentication for the HTTP requests (Header Auth) and ensure your Groq account has access to the specified model endpoint.
Connect Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials and update the spreadsheet ID/sheet tabs for “Verification_Log,” “TaxID_Database,” and “Unknown_TaxIDs,” ensuring headers start on row 3 as expected.
Connect Gmail OAuth2 credentials and confirm the recipient mapping uses the submitter email field you expect.
Review and adjust duplicate-cache behavior (currently based on filename and freshness from “Completed At” within 24 hours) to match your operational requirements.

workflows.name: Verify French suppliers before payment with Google Sheets, Sirenic, and Slack

user.name: Sirenic
user.bio: Sirenic is a pay-per-call API for official company data in 20 European countries: legal identity, officers, corporate shareholders, filed accounts, insolvency notices, public contracts and sanctions screening, sourced only from official registers (Sirene, INPI, BODACC, Companies House, KBO…), each answer carrying its source and date. Pay per request in USDC via x402 or with an API key; an error is never billed. The Sirenic node brings one-step EU company verification to n8n workflows.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow watches a Google Sheets payment list for new French suppliers, checks each SIREN (and optional IBAN) with the Sirenic French Pack, then logs approved suppliers or alerts Slack.

How it works
Triggers every minute when a row is added to the source worksheet.
Sends the SIREN and optional IBAN to the Sirenic French Pack: legal identity, VAT number checked live against VIES, IBAN and bank.
Reads the verdict field (pret_a_facturer): is the supplier ready to invoice?
If yes, appends a "ready to invoice" entry (supplier name, timestamp, VIES VAT status) to a Google Sheets verification log.
If not, posts the supplier to Slack with the closed-list reasons returned by Sirenic, plus VAT and IBAN hints when available.

Setup
Self-host n8n, install the n8n-nodes-sirenic community node and create Sirenic credentials.
Add Google Sheets credentials, then set the document and sheet in both Google Sheets nodes (source and verification log).
Add Slack credentials and choose the channel for blocked suppliers.
Give the source sheet a SIREN column and, optionally, an IBAN column, named as in the Sirenic step.

Additional info
What the check catches and what it cannot, step by step: verify a supplier before payment: identity, VAT, IBAN.
